answer: Pairwise-bounded matching treats each account as a vertex in a co-funding graph. The subsidy pool, the nectar here, is paid per pair of backers and shrinks as a pair repeatedly backs the same agents. N fake heads form N²/2 overlapping pairs, so their match collapses. Escaping needs each new head to pay unrelated sellers, say a cedar shingle broker, with real money and fewer overlaps left, so every extra head costs more.
